entities.name: PMID:25099519
observations: In orthotopic MDA-MB-231 luc-D3H2LN xenografts, blocking tumor-cell α9β1 reduced tumor growth, lymphatic metastasis, CAF recruitment, and host-derived osteopontin.
Wild-type but not OPN-deficient fibroblasts enhanced tumor growth when co-inoculated, supporting a CAF-derived OPN effector mechanism.

entities.name: PMID:22545097
observations: In MDA-MB-468LN breast cancer cells, α9β1 and tumor-cell VEGF-D jointly promoted invasion, lymphatic endothelial activation, intratumoral lymphangiogenesis, and lymphatic metastasis.
Knockdown of either α9 or VEGF-D abrogated the in-vivo lymphangiogenesis/metastasis phenotype; CAF recruitment and CAF necessity were not tested.

entities.name: ITGA9
observations: Tumor-cell α9 integrin, paired with β1, is required for the reported breast-cancer growth and lymphatic-metastasis phenotypes in the cited xenograft models.

entities.name: SPP1
observations: Host/CAF-derived osteopontin functionally contributed to tumor growth in the α9β1-positive MDA-MB-231 xenograft model.

entities.name: VEGFD
observations: Tumor-cell VEGF-D cooperated with α9β1 to promote lymphangiogenesis and lymphatic metastasis in MDA-MB-468LN xenografts; this branch was not shown to require CAFs.

entities.name: Cancer-associated fibroblasts
observations: CAF recruitment and CAF-derived OPN were supported downstream of tumor-cell α9β1 in one orthotopic breast-cancer xenograft model; CAF mediation was not tested in the independent VEGF-D study.

entities.name: α9β1-CAF-OPN axis
observations: Tumor-cell α9β1 signaling supports CAF recruitment or activation-like stromal function, with CAF-derived OPN promoting breast-tumor growth and lymphatic metastasis in an orthotopic xenograft model.

entities.name: α9β1-VEGF-D lymphangiogenesis
observations: A separate breast-cancer model supports tumor-cell α9β1 cooperation with VEGF-D in lymphatic endothelial activation, lymphangiogenesis, and lymphatic metastasis, independently of demonstrated CAF causality.
